name: Greyish Violet-Blue
lede: Greyish Violet-Blue is a muted, slate-leaning blue named by modifier grammar as greyish plus [[violet-blue]], placed on Ridgway's 1912 color plates and filed in the ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 under its American spelling, Grayish Violet-Blue.

sections.title: Greyish, plus violet-blue
sections.body:
Robert Ridgway, an American ornithologist, gave this hue plate XXIV, hue 53*, tone i, in his 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature*, a scan of an aged printed page and so only approximate [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary of 1955 later filed the same hue, spelled the American way as Grayish Violet-Blue, at block 211 [1][2].

The nearest named look-alikes on file are [[sailor-blue|Sailor Blue]], more vivid, and [[deep-soft-blue-violet|Deep Soft Blue-Violet]], also more vivid [3]. [[azure-blue|Azure Blue]] sits further off, duller and bluer [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
In our 23,781-painting archive, 73 paintings carry a color close enough to this one over enough of their canvas to count, 0.31 per cent, as photographed, rarer than 59 per cent of our named colors [4]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, by lightness rank, in 50 per cent of the 24 paintings where that lens applies, so varnish cannot fake the reading [4].

It peaks in the 1900s, found in 0.5 per cent of the 1,674 paintings we have from that century (9 paintings), 3.4 times the expected rate [4]. The earliest match is dated 1420, in a work attributed to Fra Angelico, though the archive's thin early centuries make that a floor on when the hue appears, not a first sighting, and 492 years before Ridgway's 1912 record of the name [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment matches [4].
